reason: E1 supports the general concept that an inverted BCC+B2 microstructure improves ductility in RHEAs, but it concerns a different alloy (AlNbTaTiVZr) and does not provide evidence for NbMoTaW, the specific heat treatment proposed, or the preservation of high-temperature strength and irradiation resistance. E2 describes a different processing route and alloy, offering no direct support for the key premises about NbMoTaW.
premises: Inverted BCC+B2 microstructure with discrete B2 in continuous BCC improves room-temperature ductility in RHEAs
The ductility improvement mechanism applies to NbMoTaW
The heat treatment (1400°C solutionize + 600°C/120h anneal + quench) produces discrete B2 precipitates in a continuous BCC matrix in NbMoTaW
High-temperature yield strength (~400 MPa at 1600°C) is preserved with this microstructure
Irradiation resistance is unaltered by the discrete B2 precipitates
